title: Echelon App Does Not Connect to Bike
shortDescription: FitPass app cannot detect or pair with Echelon equipment.
fullDescription:
Echelon bikes use Bluetooth LE to communicate cadence, resistance, and heart rate to the FitPass app. Failed pairing is usually due to Bluetooth being off on the phone, an app that needs updating, or another paired device hogging the signal.

Force-closing the app and re-pairing with Bluetooth freshly toggled almost always clears it.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Turn phone Bluetooth off, wait 10 seconds, back on.

fixSteps.title: Update app
fixSteps.instruction: Install the latest FitPass app from the App Store or Play Store.

fixSteps.title: Force close
fixSteps.instruction: Fully close the app and reopen, then scan for the bike.

whenToCallPro: Call Echelon support if none of the troubleshooting steps resolve the issue.

faq.a: Only the app needs Wi-Fi or cellular - the bike uses Bluetooth to the phone.

title: Echelon Resistance Feels Too Light or Too Heavy
shortDescription: Displayed resistance does not match actual flywheel resistance.
fullDescription: Over time, the magnet assembly in Echelon bikes can drift from the flywheel due to vibration. This makes resistance level 30 feel like level 15 or vice versa. A simple manual calibration of the resistance knob and screw restores expected feel.

fixSteps.title: Remove side cover
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the plastic cover on the side of the frame to access the magnet bracket.

fixSteps.title: Adjust bracket
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen the bracket screw and slide the magnets closer to the flywheel. Retest.

whenToCallPro: Call Echelon if adjustment does not restore expected feel.

faq.q: Can I see resistance on bike?
faq.a: No, resistance is only shown in the FitPass app.

title: Echelon Cadence Not Showing in App
shortDescription: RPM stays at zero in FitPass despite pedaling.
fullDescription: The cadence sensor is a small reed switch near the crank. A loose wire or misaligned magnet stops cadence reporting. Since it uses the same Bluetooth connection as resistance, the app often still shows the bike connected, just with 0 RPM.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Remove plastic crank cover and check magnet is secure on the crank.

fixSteps.title: Reseat wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and replug the sensor wire.

whenToCallPro: Call if magnet and wiring look good but RPM still zero.

faq.a: You can still ride, but cadence-based classes will not score.

title: Echelon Auto-Follow Resistance Not Adjusting
shortDescription: Resistance does not change automatically during classes.
fullDescription: Auto-follow uses a two-way Bluetooth channel that not all Echelon models support. Confirm the model has auto-follow and that it is enabled in settings. Weak Bluetooth signal from device placement can also prevent the commands from reaching the bike.
symptoms: Class shows target but bike does not match

fixSteps.title: Enable in app
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Equipment > Auto-Resistance and toggle on.

fixSteps.title: Move device closer
fixSteps.instruction: Keep phone or tablet within 3 feet of the bike.

whenToCallPro: If auto-follow is supposed to work but never does, contact Echelon support.

faq.a: No, only EX-5s and above support auto resistance.

title: Echelon Heart Rate Monitor Not Pairing
shortDescription: FitPass does not detect Bluetooth chest strap.
fullDescription: FitPass supports Bluetooth LE heart rate monitors. Dead battery, active pairing with another app, or dry chest contacts prevent connection.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect other apps
fixSteps.instruction: Close Strava, Garmin Connect or any other app that may be holding the HRM.

faq.a: Apple Watch does not broadcast BLE HR unless a workout app is open - use a chest strap for reliability.

title: Echelon Pedal Clicking or Creaking
shortDescription: Rhythmic click or creak from crank area during pedaling.
fullDescription: Creaking noises usually come from loose pedals, a loose crank arm, or dry bearings. Tightening pedals and the crank bolt usually fixes it.

fixSteps.title: Tighten pedals
fixSteps.instruction: Right pedal tightens clockwise, left pedal counter-clockwise.

fixSteps.title: Tighten crank bolt
fixSteps.instruction: Pop off the dust cap and snug crank bolt to spec.

whenToCallPro: Call if noise persists after tightening - may be bearings.

faq.q: Can I use my own pedals?
faq.a: Yes, standard 9/16 pedals fit Echelon bikes.

title: Echelon Small Display Not Showing Data
shortDescription: Built-in LCD on some models is blank or frozen.
fullDescription: Echelon bikes with built-in LCDs (EX-3s, EX-5s) depend on the battery in the console. A fresh set of AA batteries usually restores the display.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: If corroded, clean with isopropyl alcohol.

title: Echelon FitPass Subscription Login Error
shortDescription: App reports subscription expired or invalid.
fullDescription: FitPass subscription issues appear when billing fails or the account session has expired. Verify subscription in account settings and re-login.

fixSteps.title: Check billing
fixSteps.instruction: Log in at echelonfit.com and review subscription status.

fixSteps.title: Re-login
fixSteps.instruction: Sign out of FitPass app and sign back in.

whenToCallPro: Call Echelon billing for payment disputes.

faq.a: Yes, scenic and freestyle rides work without FitPass.

title: Echelon Smart Rower Stroke Count Incorrect
shortDescription: Stroke rate reading off or skipping strokes.
fullDescription: Stroke sensor issues on the Smart Rower are usually due to a loose connection at the handle or flywheel sensor. Inspect the cable run and reseat connectors.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cabling
fixSteps.instruction: Check the sensor cable along the rail for kinks.

whenToCallPro: If cable is intact but still failing, call Echelon.
videoSearchQuery: Echelon Smart Rower stroke count fix

faq.a: No user calibration is available - sensor must report correctly.

title: Echelon Bike Wobbles During Riding
shortDescription: Bike rocks side to side or floor feet unstable.
fullDescription: Wobble is usually leveling feet not adjusted or loose base bolts after initial assembly. Check all frame bolts and adjust the leveling feet so all four contact the floor evenly.

fixSteps.title: Adjust feet
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate the adjustable feet until all four touch firmly.

fixSteps.title: Retorque bolts
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten all frame bolts per the manual's torque spec.

faq.a: Yes, a dense rubber mat helps with both stability and floor protection.
